title: Inspiring the Next Space Pioneers, Innovators, Researchers, and Explorers (INSPIRE) Women Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the House passed version is repeated here.)

Inspiring the Next Space Pioneers, Innovators, Researchers, and Explorers (INSPIRE) Women Act

(Sec. 3) This bill directs the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) to encourage women and girls to study science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), pursue careers in aerospace, and further advance the nation's space science and exploration efforts through support of the following initiatives:

  • NASA GIRLS and NASA BOYS;
  • Aspire to Inspire; and
  • Summer Institute in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Research.

(Sec. 4) NASA shall submit to Congress a specified plan on how NASA can best facilitate and support both current and retired astronauts, scientists, engineers, and innovators, including early career female astronauts, scientists, engineers, and innovators, to engage with K-12 female STEM students and inspire the next generation of women to consider participating in STEM fields and to pursue careers in aerospace.

summary.headline: A 2017 law directs NASA to encourage women and girls to study STEM subjects and pursue aerospace careers, and requires a plan for role models to help.
summary.what_it_does: The law tells NASA to encourage women and girls to study science, technology, engineering, and math and to pursue careers in aerospace. It names three existing or planned programs NASA should support: NASA GIRLS and NASA BOYS, Aspire to Inspire, and the Summer Institute in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Research. It also requires NASA to send Congress a plan for how current and retired astronauts, scientists, engineers, and innovators, including early career women, can engage with K-12 female STEM students.

who_it_affects.group: K-12 girls interested in science, technology, engineering, and math
who_it_affects.how: NASA is directed to support outreach programs and activities aimed at encouraging them to pursue STEM studies and aerospace careers.

who_it_affects.group: Women working or training in STEM and aerospace fields
who_it_affects.how: The plan is meant to connect early career women with female K-12 students as possible mentors and role models.

who_it_affects.group: Current and retired NASA astronauts, scientists, engineers, and innovators
who_it_affects.how: NASA must plan for how they can take part in outreach to K-12 female students.
The agency must run or support the named programs and prepare and submit the required plan to Congress.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted February 28, 2017. The summary does not list a separate effective date or deadline for the required plan.
